reading2.title: A Return Ticket to Dammam
reading2.text:
Mansour is at the railway station in Riyadh. He wants to visit his uncle in Dammam. The train is fast and easy, and the journey is about four hours.
Mansour: Good morning. Can I have a ticket to Dammam, please?
Man: Single or return?
Mansour: Return, please. I come back on Saturday.
Man: That's 150 riyals.
Mansour: Can I pay by card?
Man: Yes, of course.
Mansour: What time is the next train?
Man: At ten o'clock. It goes from platform 3.
Mansour: Thank you. And where's the café, please?
Man: It's over there, next to platform 1.

reading.title: My Grandfather's Childhood
reading.text:
My grandfather was born in 1950 in a small village near Al-Ahsa. His childhood was very different from my childhood.

reading.text:
Talal is nineteen. He is a student at IATC, and he is the college chess champion. He can play chess really well. He started when he was eight, and now he plays online every evening.

reading.text:

reading.title: A Bad Day
reading.text:
Yesterday was a bad day for Hamad. In the morning, he missed the bus to college. Then the ticket machine at the metro station was broken. He was late for class.
At lunch, he played football and had a small accident. He fell down and hurt his arm. 'What's the matter?' asked his friend. 'My arm hurts,' said Hamad. They went to the college clinic. It wasn't broken.
In the evening, there was another problem. Hamad couldn't find his passport anywhere! He was very worried. Then his mother found it in his jacket. 'What a day!' he said.
comp: Why was Hamad late for class?
He missed the bus and the ticket machine was broken.
How did he hurt his arm?
tf: They went to the college clinic.

reading.title: Shops Near the College
reading.text:
There are many shops around our college. Next to the main gate, there is a small bookshop. You can buy dictionaries, notebooks and pens there.
Opposite the bookshop, there is a coffee shop. It opens at seven, so you can get a coffee before class. Near the coffee shop, there is a bakery. The bread is fresh and cheap.
There is also a pharmacy. You can buy medicine, shampoo and conditioner there. And there is a cash machine outside the supermarket.
In the supermarket, you can buy everything: cereal, beans, fruit and drinks. Pay at the till.

Assistant: Good morning. Can I help you?

Assistant: Would you like small eggs or large eggs?

reading.title: Signs at the Airport
reading.text:
Airports have many signs. Can you understand them?
At the entrance, there are two doors. One door says PUSH and the other says PULL. Inside, you can see the sign NO SMOKING. You can't smoke in the airport.
Next to the lift, there is a sign: OUT OF ORDER. The lift isn't working, so take the stairs. A door near the toilets says STAFF ONLY. Passengers can't go in.
At the gate, a sign says PLEASE WAIT HERE. Another sign says DON'T FORGET YOUR BAGS. In the hangar, a sign says NO PHOTOS. You can't take photos there. In an emergency, follow the green EXIT signs.
comp: What can't you do in the airport?
Why do you take the stairs?
Because the lift is out of order.
What signs do you follow in an emergency?
tf: You can't smoke in the airport.
Passengers can go through the STAFF ONLY door.
You can take photos in the hangar.

days.grammarTitle: too much • too many • comparatives: smaller
days.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to give five pieces of health advice using too much / too many and one comparative adjective.

rules: too much + uncountable: too much sugar, too much salt
too many + plural: too many sweets, too many crisps
Short adjectives + er / est: small → smaller → the smallest
examples: Don't eat too much sugar.
He drinks too many fizzy drinks.
Eat smaller meals in the evening.
practice: There's too ___ salt in this soup. (much / many)

reading.title: Running the Marathon
reading.text:
Last year, my uncle Faisal ran the Riyadh Marathon. A marathon is 42 kilometres! He was very happy when he crossed the finish line.
Faisal is fifty years old, but he is very active. He gets up at dawn and runs ten kilometres before work. In the evening, after sunset, he rides his bike in the park.
He has a healthy diet. He eats a lot of fruit and vegetables. 'Don't eat too much sugar, and don't eat too many sweets,' he tells me. 'Eat smaller meals and drink a lot of water. Then you have more energy and you feel great!'
comp: What does he do after sunset?
He rides his bike in the park.
tf: Faisal ran the Riyadh Marathon last year.
He runs ten kilometres before work.
He eats a lot of sweets.
He says drink a lot of water.

reading.text:
Hi Mum,
I'm writing this message on the train. I'm travelling to Qassim with my friends Majed and Nawaf. We're using public transport because the roads are busy. There's a big traffic jam on the motorway!

reading.text:
Last month, Nawaf travelled to Europe with his brother. They used four kinds of transport in seven days.

In France, they travelled by train. The train went through a long tunnel under the sea to London. Then they took a bus along the river.
At the end, they went on a short cruise across the sea. Nawaf carried his rucksack everywhere. 'Next year,' he says, 'I want to go into the desert by jeep!'

grammar.title: The Verb To Be
grammar.sub: am  •  is  •  are  •  I'm  •  he's  •  they're
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use am / is / are and the short forms (I'm, he's, they're) correctly in affirmative sentences, negative sentences, Yes / No questions and Wh- questions about names, age, countries, jobs and feelings, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.

write about myself in about 25 words.

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: isn't = is not      aren't = are not      We say “I'm not”, NOT “I amn't”.

grammar.overviewTitle: When Do We Use am / is / are?
overview: My bag is in the car.
rules: Affirmative (+)
Subject + am / is / are + …
He {is} a police officer.
Negative (−)
Subject + am not / isn't / aren't + …
The coffee {isn't} hot.
Yes / No question (?)
Am / Is / Are + subject + …?
{Are} you from Riyadh?  —  Yes, I am.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + am / is / are + subject?
Where {is} he from?  —  He's from Egypt.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ He doctor.   ✓ He {is} a doctor.      ✗ I have 19 years.   ✓ I {am} 19 years old.
grammar.watchNote: Arabic has no present-tense 'be' in sentences like هو طبيب, so students often drop it. Age uses be (I'm 19), not have. Say every example aloud and tap the table on am / is / are.

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: Subject  +  am / is / are  +  noun / adjective / place          I'm  •  he's  •  we're  •  they're

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: Subject  +  am not / isn't / aren't  +  …
items: My brother {isn't} a doctor. He's a nurse.
It {isn't} cold in Riyadh in September.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Am / Is / Are  +  subject  +  …?      Short answer:  Yes, I am.  /  No, it isn't.
items: {Are} you a student? — Yes, I am.
{Is} he from Egypt? — Yes, he is.
{Is} your house big? — No, it isn't. It's small.
{Are} they from England? — No, they aren't. They're from Canada.
{Is} the coffee hot? — Yes, it is.
{Are} we in class FND 68? — Yes, we are.
{Is} your father a doctor? — No, he isn't. He's a teacher.
{Is} Fahad from Jeddah? — No, he isn't. He's from Riyadh.
{Is} London in England? — Yes, it is.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  am / is / are  +  subject  +  …?          What's = What is      Where's = Where is
items: What{'s} your name? — My name's Khalid.
Where {are} you from? — I'm from Saudi Arabia.
Who {is} your English teacher? — Mr Adel is my teacher.
What{'s} this in English? — It's a camera.
What{'s} your job? — I'm a student.
Where{'s} your house? — It's near the college.
What colour {is} your car? — It's white.
How many students {are} in your class? — There are 28 students.

practice: They ____ from Spain. They're from Italy.
____ he from Egypt?  Yes, he is.
We ____ at home. We are in class.
The coffee ____ hot. It is cold.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the am / is / are table and redo the items they missed.

grammar.title: The Present Simple
grammar.sub: I get up  •  She gets up  •  I always / never …
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the present simple (verb / verb-s, don't / doesn't, do / does) and the adverbs of frequency always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever and never in the correct position to talk about daily routines, free time, food and likes, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: talk about my day and my free time.
add -s / -es / -ies after he, she and it.
make negatives with don't and doesn't.
ask and answer with do and does.
use always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever, never.
ask and answer: How often …?
warmup: What time do you get up?
What do you have for breakfast?
What do you do at the weekend?

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: don't = do not      doesn't = does not      After don't / doesn't / do / does → verb with NO -s:  He doesn't play.  Does he play?

grammar.overviewTitle: When Do We Use the Present Simple?
overview: I get up at six every day.
rules: Affirmative (+)
I / you / we / they + verb      he / she / it + verb-s
She {gets} up at seven o'clock.
Negative (−)
Subject + don't / doesn't + verb
He {doesn't} eat meat.
Yes / No question (?)
Do / Does + subject + verb …?
{Do} you like tennis?  —  Yes, I do.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + do / does + subject + verb?
What time {does} he get home?  —  At six.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ I am like tea.   ✓ I {like} tea.      ✗ She get up at 7.   ✓ She {gets} up at 7.
grammar.watchNote: Three common errors: (1) adding 'am / is / are' before a present-simple verb (I am like); (2) forgetting -s with he / she / it (She get up); (3) the adverb in the wrong place (✗ I go always to bed at 11 → ✓ I always go to bed at 11). Also: no -s after doesn't / does (✗ He doesn't plays).

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: I / You / We / They  +  verb          He / She / It  +  verb-s
items: I {get up} at six o'clock every day.
He {has} a shower in the morning.
My mother {watches} a drama on TV.
They {live} in a flat in Riyadh.
My uncle {goes} shopping at the weekend.

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: I / You / We / They  +  don't  +  verb          He / She / It  +  doesn't  +  verb
items: We {don't} go to college on Friday.
They {don't} live in a big house.
I {don't} watch TV in the morning.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Do / Does  +  subject  +  verb …?      Short answer:  Yes, I do.  /  No, he doesn't.
items: {Do} you like pizza? — Yes, I do. I love it!
{Does} your father work all day? — Yes, he does.
{Do} you play tennis? — No, I don't. I play football.
{Does} she speak Japanese? — No, she doesn't.
{Do} you live in a flat? — Yes, I do.
{Does} your mother cook kabsa? — Yes, she does. It's delicious!
{Do} they go out on Thursday? — Yes, they do.
{Does} the bus stop here? — No, it doesn't.
{Do} you have breakfast at home? — Yes, I do.
{Does} your brother drive to work? — No, he doesn't. He takes a taxi.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  do / does  +  subject  +  verb …?
items: What time {do} you get up? — I get up at six o'clock.
What {do} you have for breakfast? — Eggs, toast and tea.
Where {does} your aunt live? — She lives in Jeddah.
What time {does} your father get home? — At five o'clock.
What {do} you do at the weekend? — I visit my family and relax.
How many languages {do} you speak? — Two: Arabic and English.
What {does} your brother do? — He's a waiter. He works in a restaurant.
When {do} you go to bed? — At eleven o'clock.
What sports {do} you like? — I like swimming and football.
Who {cooks} dinner in your house? — My mother cooks dinner.

sections.title: Adverbs of Frequency: 10 Examples
sections.formula: Subject  +  adverb  +  verb …          Subject  +  am / is / are  +  adverb …
items: I {always} have a shower in the morning.
My mother {usually} cooks kabsa on Friday.
My brother {sometimes} drives me to work.
My father is {never} late for work.
We {usually} go shopping at the weekend.
They {often} watch TV in the evening.

sections.title: How Often …? Questions and Answers
sections.formula: How often  +  do / does  +  subject  +  verb …?      every day • once a week • twice a week • on Fridays
items: How often {do} you play football? — Twice a week.
How often {does} he go shopping? — Once a week, on Thursday.
How often {do} you visit your uncle? — Every Friday.
How often {do} you eat pizza? — Hardly ever. I like kabsa!
How often {does} your mother cook? — Every day.
How often {do} they go to the beach? — Two or three times a year.
How often {do} you watch TV? — Sometimes, in the evening.
How often {does} the bus come? — Every twenty minutes.
How often {do} you have English? — Five days a week.
How often {does} your brother go out? — Once or twice a week.

practice: ____ you like pizza?  Yes, I do.
____ your father work all day?  No, he doesn't.
What time ____ he go to bed?
Add never:  He drinks coffee at night.
He never drinks coffee at night.
Add always:  I am busy on Sunday.
I am always busy on Sunday.
How ____ do you go shopping?  Once a week.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the form table (items 1–7) or the 'Where does the adverb go?' slide (items 8–10) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: when you get up and have breakfast
what you do in the afternoon
what you usually do at the weekend
exit.frame: I always get up at ____. I usually have ____ for breakfast. In the afternoon, I ____. At the weekend, I sometimes ____.
exit.model: I always get up at six. I usually have eggs for breakfast. In the afternoon, I study English. At the weekend, I sometimes visit my uncle. (26 words)

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A1 Grammar/FND_68_A1_Grammar_4_Present_Simple_Headway.pptx

grammar.title: Possessives & have / has
grammar.sub: my  •  his  •  Fatima's  •  mine  •  I have / he has
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use possessive adjectives (my, his, their), possessive 's, possessive pronouns (mine, yours) and have / has correctly to talk about their family and friends, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: use my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun.
use 's for family: Fatima's husband.
use mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.
ask and answer Whose …? questions.
use have / has for family and things.
write about my family in about 25 words.
warmup: How many brothers do you have?

head: Subject
Possessive adj.
Possessive pronoun
Example
rows: We have a cat. Its name is Max.
table.note: its = belongs to it (no apostrophe)      it's = it is      Possessive adjective + noun:  my phone.   Possessive pronoun alone:  mine.

rules: Possessive adjective
my / your / his / her / its / our / their + noun
This is {my} family.
Possessive 's
name / noun + 's + noun
Adel is {Fatima's} husband.
Possessive pronoun
mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs  (no noun after)
The black bag is {mine}.
Whose …?
Whose + noun + is this / are these?
{Whose} phone is this?  —  It's Talal's.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ This is mine phone.  ✓ This is {my} phone.     ✗ the son of Adel  ✓ {Adel's} son
grammar.watchNote: Arabic shows possession with a suffix (هاتفي) or with idafa (ابن عادل), so students often say 'the son of Adel' or 'mine phone'. Practise: in English the owner comes first (Adel's son). Also: 's can mean is (He's my brother = He is) or show possession (Talal's bag). Context tells you which.

sections.title: Possessive Adjectives + Noun
sections.formula: my  /  your  /  his  /  her  /  its  /  our  /  their   +   noun
items: {Your} English book is on the desk.
My brother is 21. {His} name is Turki.
My aunt is a doctor. {Her} hospital is big.
We have a white cat. {Its} name is Max.
My uncles live in Jeddah. {Their} flat is big.
My father reads {his} newspaper every day.

sections.title: Possessive 's: Fatima's Family
sections.formula: Name / noun  +  's  +  noun          Plural owner (-s):  my parents' house
items: The {teacher's} desk is next to the board.
My {parents'} house is near the park.

sections.title: Possessive Pronouns
sections.formula: mine  /  yours  /  his  /  hers  /  ours  /  theirs        (NO noun after)
items: My car is white. {Yours} is black.
Your phone is new. {Mine} is old.

sections.title: Whose …? Questions
sections.formula: Whose  +  noun  +  is this / are these?        Answer:  It's Talal's.  /  It's mine.
items: {Whose} shoes are these? — They're my brother's.
{Whose} book is on the desk? — It's the teacher's.
{Whose} car is that? — It's my father's.
Is this {your} pen? — Yes, it's mine.
Is this {his} jacket? — No, it isn't. It's mine.
What's {your} father's job? — He's an accountant.
What's {your} best friend's name? — His name is Abdullah.
Where's {their} house? — It's near the bank.

sections.title: have / has: Family and Things
sections.formula: I / you / we / they  +  have          he / she / it  +  has          −  don't have / doesn't have
items: I {have} two brothers and a sister.
My best friend {has} a lot of friends.
My brother {doesn't have} a job yet.
{Do} you {have} a laptop?  —  Yes, I do.

practice: My brother is 21. ____ name is Turki.
We are a big family. ____ house is big.
Is this book ____? (you)  Yes, it's mine.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the possessives table (items 1–8) or the have / has slide (items 9–10) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: how many brothers and sisters you have
exit.frame: My father's name is ____. He is a ____. I have ____ brothers and ____ sisters. My best friend's name is ____.
exit.model: My father's name is Saleh. He is an accountant. I have two brothers and one sister. My best friend's name is Abdullah. He is funny. (25 words)

grammar.title: Plurals & There is / are
grammar.sub: rooms  •  There are some pens.  •  Are there any …?
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to form regular and irregular plurals and use there is / there are with some / any and How many …? to talk about rooms, furniture and their home town, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: make plurals with -s, -es, -ies and -ves.
use irregular plurals: men, people, children.
say what is in a room with there is / are.
use some (+) and any (− and ?).
ask and answer How many … are there?
write about my home in about 25 words.
warmup: How many rooms are there in your house?
Is there a park near your house?

head: Number
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: There's = There is      some → + sentences      any → − and ? sentences      a / an → one thing

rules: Plural noun
noun + s / es / ies / ves   (or irregular)
two {rooms},  three {buses},  five {people}
There is / There are
There is + a / an + one thing   •   There are + plural
{There are} four bedrooms in our house.
some (+)
There are some + plural noun
There are {some} pens in the drawer.
any (− and ?)
There aren't any …  /  Are there any …?
{Are there any} books?  —  No, there aren't.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ There is two bedrooms.  ✓ {There are} two bedrooms.      ✗ two childs  ✓ two {children}
grammar.watchNote: Arabic uses يوجد for one thing and for many things, so students say 'There is two …'. Count the noun first: one → is, two or more → are. Irregular plurals never take -s (✗ childs, ✗ peoples).

sections.title: Plural Nouns
sections.formula: room → rooms      bus → buses      city → cities      shelf → shelves      man → men
items: There are two {bathrooms} in our house.
The {walls} in my bedroom are white.
My {car keys} are on the table.
There are many {people} in the park.

sections.title: There is / There are: My Home
sections.formula: There is  +  a / an  +  singular noun          There are  +  plural noun
items: {There is} a sofa in the living room.
{There are} four bedrooms in our house.
{There is} a cooker in the kitchen.
{There are} two lamps next to the bed.
{There is} an armchair in my room.
{There are} some posters on the wall.
{There is} a big park in my home town.
{There is} a library near the college.

sections.title: some / any
sections.formula: +   There are some …          −   There aren't any …          ?   Are there any …?
items: There are {some} pens in the drawer.
There aren't {any} books on the desk.
There is {some} water in the fridge.
There isn't {any} milk in the fridge.
There are {some} good shops in my town.

sections.title: Is there …? / Are there any …? / How many …?
sections.formula: Is there a …?  Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.       Are there any …?  Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
items: {Is there} a TV in your bedroom? — No, there isn't.
{Are there} any pens in the drawer? — Yes, there are.
{Is there} a garden at your house? — Yes, there is.
{Are there} any posters on the wall? — No, there aren't.
{Is there} any water in the fridge? — Yes, there is.
{Are there} any parks near your house? — Yes, there are two.
{Is there} a supermarket near here? — Yes, there is. It's on the left.
{How many} rooms are there in your flat? — There are five.
{How many} people are there in your family? — There are seven.
{Are there} any museums in Riyadh? — Yes, there are. The National Museum!

practice: There ____ four bedrooms in our house.
There ____ a sofa in the living room.
There are ____ pens in the drawer. (+)
Are there ____ books?  No, there aren't.
How ____ rooms are there?  There are six.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the plural spelling rules (items 1–5) or the there is / are table (items 6–10) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: what there is in your bedroom
what there is near your home
exit.frame: I live in a ____. There are ____ rooms. In my bedroom, there is a ____ and some ____. Near my home, there is a ____.
exit.model: I live in a flat in Riyadh. There are five rooms. In my bedroom, there is a desk and some books. Near my home, there is a park. (28 words)

grammar.title: Place & Time Prepositions
grammar.sub: in  •  on  •  under  •  next to      at  •  on  •  in
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use in, on, under, next to, between, behind, in front of and opposite for place, at home / at work, and at, on, in for time, correctly in sentences and in Where …? / When …? questions about their home, town and week, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: say where things are: in, on, under, next to.
use between, behind, in front of, opposite.
use at home, at work, at college.
use at, on, in with times, days, months, seasons.
ask and answer Where …? and When …?
write about my week in about 25 words.
warmup: What time do you get up?
What do you do at the weekend?

head: Preposition
Place
Time
Arabic
table.note: Time:  at + clock time, night, the weekend      on + day, date      in + month, season, year, the morning / afternoon / evening

rules: Place: in / on / under
in = inside   •   on = on top   •   under = below
The pens are {in} the drawer.
Place: next to / between / opposite
next to = beside   •   between = in the middle of two
The bank is {between} the café and the hotel.
Time: at / on
at + clock time, night, the weekend   •   on + day, date
I get up {at} 6 o'clock {on} Sunday.
Time: in
in + month, season, year, the morning
It's very hot {in} summer.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ in Sunday  ✓ {on} Sunday     ✗ on 8 o'clock  ✓ {at} 8 o'clock     ✗ in night  ✓ {at} night
grammar.watchNote: Arabic uses في for in, on and at with time (في يوم الأحد، في الساعة الثامنة), so students choose 'in' for everything. Draw the time triangle: at (small: clock time) → on (days, dates) → in (big: months, seasons, years, parts of the day). Places: at home / at work / at college (no 'the'), but in Riyadh, in the kitchen.

sections.title: Place: in / on / under / next to …
sections.formula: in   •   on   •   under   •   next to   •   between   •   behind   •   in front of   •   opposite
items: The DVD player is {under} the TV.
The lamp is {next to} the bed.
My car keys are {in} the drawer.
The bank is {between} the café and the hotel.
The bus stops {in front of} the museum.
There are some posters {on} the wall.

sections.title: Time: at / on / in
sections.formula: at + time          on + day / date          in + month / season / year / the morning
items: The bus comes {at} half past seven.
We go to the desert {in} winter.

sections.title: Where …? Questions
sections.formula: Where is / are + noun?        →        It's / They're  +  in / on / under / next to …    •    at home / at work
items: {Where} is my phone? — It's on the sofa.
{Where} are my car keys? — They're in the drawer.
{Where} is the cat? — It's under the bed.
{Where} is the bank? — It's between the café and the hotel.
{Where} do you live? — I live in a flat in Riyadh.
{Where} is your father? — He's at work.
{Where} are your brothers? — They're at home.
{Where} do you study? — I study at college.
{Where} is the bus station? — It's opposite the supermarket.
{Where} is the lamp? — It's next to the bed.

sections.title: When …? / What time …? Questions
sections.formula: When / What time  +  is / do / does  …?        →        at / on / in  …
items: {When} is Progress Exam 2? — It's in October.
{What time} do you get up? — At six o'clock.
{When} do you play football? — On Friday.
{When} do you study English? — In the afternoon.
{What time} does the bus come? — At half past seven.
{When} is Saudi National Day? — It's on 23 September.
{When} do you relax? — At the weekend.
{When} is it cold in Riyadh? — In winter.
{When} do you do your homework? — In the evening.
{What time} do you go to bed? — At eleven o'clock.

practice: The bank is ____ the café and the hotel.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the place rules (items 1–5) or the time triangle (items 6–10) and redo the items they missed.

exit.frame: I get up at ____. On Friday, I ____. I study at ____ in the ____.
exit.model: I get up at six o'clock. On Friday, I visit my grandfather. I study at college in the afternoon from Sunday to Thursday. (23 words)

grammar.title: Past of Be: was / were
grammar.sub: was  •  were  •  wasn't  •  weren't  •  was born
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use was / were, was born and there was / there were with past time words (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2015, when I was a child) correctly in affirmative sentences, negative sentences, Yes / No questions and Wh- questions about yesterday and their childhood, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: use was (I, he, she, it) and were (you, we, they).
use yesterday, last …, … ago, in 2015.
make negatives with wasn't and weren't.
ask and answer Was / Were …? and Wh- questions.
say where and when I was born.
write about my childhood in about 25 words.
warmup: Were you at home last night?

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: am / is → was      are → were      Time words:  yesterday  •  last night / week / year  •  two days ago  •  in 2015  •  when I was a child

rules: Affirmative (+)
Subject + was / were + …
I {was} at home yesterday.
Negative (−)
Subject + wasn't / weren't + …
The exam {wasn't} difficult.
Yes / No question (?)
Was / Were + subject + …?
{Were} you at college last week?  —  Yes, I was.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + was / were + subject?
Where {were} you born?  —  In Riyadh.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ I were tired.  ✓ I {was} tired.     ✗ I born in 2007.  ✓ I {was born} in 2007.
grammar.watchNote: Link to the present: I am → I was; he is → he was; they are → they were. 'born' always needs was / were (✗ I born). 'ago' comes AFTER the time phrase (two years ago, NOT ago two years), unlike Arabic قبل سنتين.

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: I / He / She / It  +  was          You / We / They  +  were          + yesterday / last … / … ago
items: My friends {were} at the park last night.
Our house {was} small when I was a child.
My brothers {were} in Jeddah last week.

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: Subject  +  wasn't (was not)  /  weren't (were not)  +  …
items: My father {wasn't} at work on Saturday.
The bus {wasn't} on time this morning.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Was / Were  +  subject  +  …?        Short answer:  Yes, I was.  /  No, they weren't.
items: {Were} you at college yesterday? — Yes, I was.
{Was} the exam easy? — Yes, it was.
{Was} your grandfather a teacher? — No, he wasn't. He was a farmer.
{Were} the shops open? — No, they weren't.
{Was} it hot in Riyadh yesterday? — Yes, it was. It was 40 degrees!
{Were} they at the match last night? — Yes, they were.
{Was} your first school big? — No, it wasn't. It was small.
{Were} you tired last night? — Yes, I was.
{Was} the bus late this morning? — No, it wasn't.
{Were} your friends at the mall? — Yes, they were.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  was / were  +  subject  +  …?
items: Where {were} you yesterday? — I was at home.
Where {were} you born? — I was born in Riyadh.
Who {was} your first teacher? — Mr Ali was my first teacher.
How {was} the exam? — It was easy.
Why {were} you late? — Because the bus was late.
What {was} your grandfather's job? — He was a farmer.
Where {were} you two years ago? — I was in secondary school.
What {was} the weather like yesterday? — It was hot and sunny.
How old {were} you in 2020? — I was thirteen.

sections.title: was born  •  there was / there were
sections.formula: was / were born  +  in + place / year          There was + singular          There were + plural
items: My grandfather {was born} in a village.
{There was} a small shop near my house.
{There wasn't} a park in my village.
{Was there} a school in your village?
{There were} a lot of people at the mall.

practice: The exam ____ easy. It was difficult.
____ you at college yesterday?  Yes, I was.
The shops ____ open. They were closed.
I was in Jeddah two weeks ____.
We were at the park ____ Friday.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the was / were table (items 1–6) or the past time words slide (items 7–10) and redo the items they missed.

exit.frame: I was born in ____ in ____. My house was ____. My first school was ____. My teacher was ____.
exit.model: I was born in Riyadh in 2007. My house was small and old. My first school was near my house. My teacher was kind. (24 words)

grammar.title: The Past Simple
grammar.sub: visited  •  went  •  didn't go  •  Did you go?
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use regular and irregular past simple verbs correctly in affirmative sentences, negative sentences, Yes / No questions and Wh- questions, and tell a short story with first, then, after that and finally, about their last weekend, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: add -ed to regular verbs: visited, studied, stopped.
use irregular verbs: went, had, saw, got up …
make negatives with didn't + verb.
ask Did …? and Wh- + did questions.
tell a story with first, then, after that.
write about my last weekend in about 25 words.
warmup: Where did you go last weekend?
What did you have for breakfast?
Did you watch football last night?

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: The SAME form for all subjects.   didn't = did not.   After didn't / did → base verb:   ✗ didn't went   ✓ didn't go

rules: Affirmative (+)
Subject + verb-ed  /  irregular past
I {visited} my uncle. We {went} to Abha.
Negative (−)
Subject + didn't + base verb
I {didn't} watch TV last night.
Yes / No question (?)
Did + subject + base verb …?
{Did} you have a good time?  —  Yes, I did.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + did + subject + base verb?
Where {did} you go?  —  I went to Jeddah.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ I didn't went.  ✓ I didn't {go}.     ✗ Did you saw?  ✓ Did you {see}?     ✗ I goed.  ✓ I {went}.
grammar.watchNote: After didn't / did the verb goes back to its base form (go, see, have). Irregular verbs never take -ed (goed, eated). Time words: yesterday, last …, … ago, in 2025.

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: Regular:  verb + ed  (visited, studied)          Irregular:  went, had, saw, got up …
items: We {went} to the beach in Jeddah.
My father {bought} a new car last month.
We {saw} a football match on TV.

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: Subject  +  didn't (did not)  +  base verb
items: We {didn't} go to college on Friday.
I {didn't} get up early on Saturday.
My father {didn't} buy a new phone.
I {didn't} see my friends last week.
The bus {didn't} stop at the station.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Did  +  subject  +  base verb …?        Short answer:  Yes, I did.  /  No, he didn't.
items: {Did} you have a good weekend? — Yes, I did. It was great!
{Did} you go to the beach? — No, I didn't. I went to the park.
{Did} he watch the match? — Yes, he did.
{Did} they stay at a hotel? — No, they didn't. They stayed with family.
{Did} you have breakfast this morning? — Yes, I did.
{Did} your mother cook kabsa? — Yes, she did. It was delicious!
{Did} you go shopping last week? — Yes, I did. I bought a jacket.
{Did} your brother drive to Abha? — No, he didn't. He went by bus.
{Did} you see your friends at the mall? — Yes, I did.
{Did} you study English yesterday? — Yes, I did.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  did  +  subject  +  base verb …?
items: Where {did} you go last weekend? — I went to Jeddah.
What {did} you have for breakfast? — I had eggs and toast.
What time {did} you get up? — I got up at nine o'clock.
Who {did} you meet at the mall? — I met my cousins.
How {did} you go to Jeddah? — We went by car.
What {did} you buy? — I bought a new jacket.
When {did} you get home? — At eleven o'clock.
What {did} you watch on TV? — I watched a football match.
Why {did} you stay at home? — Because I was tired.
What {did} you do last night? — I did my homework.

sections.title: My Weekend: A Story in 10 Sentences
sections.formula: First, …      Then …      After that, …      Finally, …
items: Last Friday, I {got up} at nine o'clock.
{Then} my brother {drove} us to the mall.

practice: We ____ (go) to the beach last Friday.
____ you have a good weekend?  Yes, I did.
We had lunch. ____ that, we went home.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the -ed spelling and irregular verb slides (items 1–4, 8–9) or the patterns slide (items 5–7) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: what you did first and then
exit.frame: Last weekend, I went to ____. I met ____. First, we ____. Then we ____.
exit.model: Last weekend, I went to my uncle's farm. I met my cousins there. First, we played football. Then we had kabsa for dinner. It was great! (26 words)

grammar.title: Articles a / an / the
grammar.sub: a coat  •  an apple  •  the station  •  Riyadh
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to choose a, an, the or no article correctly with jobs, shopping, places in town, meals and names, and change a → the in a short text, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: use a / an with one thing and with jobs.
choose a or an by the first sound.
use the when we know which one.
use no article with names, meals, languages.
change a → the in a short story.
write about my favourite shop in about 25 words.
warmup: What do you have for breakfast?
Is there a mall near your house?

head: Article
Use it for
Examples
Arabic
table.note: a / an + ONE thing (singular)      the + singular or plural      ✗ a books   ✓ books   ✓ the books

grammar.overviewTitle: a / an or the? Six Uses
rules: a + consonant sound
a + b, c, d, f, g … (and u = /juː/)
{a} coat,  {a} ticket,  {a} university
an + vowel sound
an + a, e, i, o, u (and silent h)
{an} apple,  {an} egg,  {an} hour
the
we know which one • only one • second time
Close {the} door, please.
No article
names, cities, countries, meals, languages, general
I live in Riyadh. I like tea.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ He is engineer.  ✓ He is {an} engineer.      ✗ I like the coffee.  ✓ I like coffee.
grammar.watchNote: Arabic has no word for a / an (هو مهندس), so students drop it: always use a / an with a job. Arabic uses ال for things in general (أحب القهوة), so students say 'I like the coffee'. In English, things in general have NO article: I like coffee. Football is exciting.

sections.title: a / an: One Thing, Jobs, How Often
sections.formula: a / an  +  one (singular) noun          jobs:  He's a waiter.          a = every:  twice a week
items: Can I have {a} packet of aspirin?
There is {an} Internet café near here.
I need {a} stamp for this postcard.
We have English five days {a} week.

sections.title: the: We Know Which One
sections.formula: the + the one we know          the + only one          a … (first time)  →  the … (second time)
items: {The} sun is very hot in summer.
I have a cat. {The} cat is white.
{The} bank is next to the hotel.

sections.title: No Article: 10 Examples
sections.formula: No article  +  names • cities • countries • languages • meals • things in general • by bus / at home
items: We have {lunch} at home on Friday.

sections.title: At the Mall: a → the
sections.formula: First time:  a / an  +  noun          Second time (now we know it):  the  +  noun
items: There is {a} new mall in my town.
In the mall, there is {a} café and {a} bookshop.
Then I see {a} jacket and {a} hat.
{The} jacket is black. {The} hat is white.
I buy {the} hat. It's only 50 riyals.

practice: I have a cat. ____ cat is white.
We have ____ lunch at one o'clock.
Excuse me, where is ____ Post Office?
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the 'a or an?' slide (items 1, 2, 7, 9), the 'Six Uses' slide (items 3, 4, 6, 10) or the 'No Article' slide (items 5, 8) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: what the shop is and where it is
what there is next to it
exit.frame: My favourite shop is a ____ in ____. It is next to a ____. The ____ are ____. I usually buy ____ there.
exit.model: My favourite shop is a bookshop in the mall. It is next to a café. The books are cheap. I usually buy a book and a coffee there. (28 words)

Here you are. Do you want a **bus tour**?
Yes, please! What can we see?
You can see the **old town** and some **ancient** **rocks**. The rocks have writing on them.
From [[eight]] in the morning until [[six]] in the evening. The bus tour is [[ninety]] riyals.
Yes. The **view** at sunset is amazing.
We came here [[ten]] years ago. It was very different then!
Yes, it's busy now. Many **tourists** come from Europe and China.

dialogues.title: Dinner at the Diner
dialogues.setting: Sunday at college. Ibrahim asks Sultan about Saturday night.
lines: Did you go out last Saturday?
Yes. My brothers and I went to a new **diner** in the mall.
Yes, we did. We sat **outside** because the weather was cool.
I had **pasta** with chicken. My brother had **roast beef**.
The pasta was great, but the roast beef was a little cold.
**Orange juice**. Then we went to a **coffee bar**.
No, I didn't. I had a **lemon** and **mint** drink.
[[Two hundred and ten]] riyals for everything.
Next time, try the **shawarma** place near my house. It's cheap!

dialogues.title: What Can a Pilot Do?
dialogues.setting: Jobs Day at college. Captain Nasser answers students' questions.
lines: Captain Nasser, what can a **pilot** do?
A pilot **can** fly a plane. I can fly a **jumbo jet**.
Yes, I can. I speak English **fluently**. All pilots need English.
No, I **can't**. That's the job of a **technician**.
I want to be an aircraft **mechanic**. I can use tools.
Good. Mechanics work in the **hangar**. They check the **wings** and the engines.
Yes. Interpreters help passengers from other countries.
Study English every day. One day, you can work at an airport too!

lines: Yes, I can. I play **really well**. I'm the college **champion**!
When I was [[eight]]. Now I play **online** every evening.
Yes, I can! Last month, I beat a player from [[Argentina]].
**A little bit**. I can't swim fast.
I can play **computer games**, but I can't play chess.
Do you want to **try**? It isn't difficult.
OK! Is it a **board game** or an online game?
Both. We can play on a board or on a **tablet**.
Let's play on a board. I like real games.

dialogues.setting: Friday evening. Majed and his father make a video call to Yousef in the US.
lines: Hello, Yousef! Can you hear me?
Yes, I can! The **Wi-Fi** is good today. I can see you clearly.
Hello, son. How is the US?
It's great, Dad. I study **mostly** in the library. Now I speak English more **fluently**.
I use the **Net** for study too. I **download** English **apps**.
Yes, every week! You write very well.
Be careful on **social media**, Majed. Don't tell anyone your **password**.
I know. And I don't **click** on strange **links**.
This **video call** is free. It's amazing!

dialogues.title: A Dangerous Sport?
dialogues.setting: The college car park. Hamad asks Bader about motor racing.
lines: Bader, is motor racing a **dangerous** sport?
It can be dangerous. The cars are very fast and very **heavy**.
Yes, I am. I always wear a strong helmet.
Do you race on city roads?
No! Fast driving on a city road is very dangerous. I only race in a **safe** place.
What do you study at college?
**Science** and **history**. I want to be an [[engineer]].
I want to design safe cars. Cars are safer now, but the driver is the most important part.
My favourite **subject** is [[geography]]. I like maps.
No, it's an easy subject. But I don't like **art**!

Oh no! Can you move it?
A little bit. It hurts a lot.
Let's go to the college clinic.
I had a small **accident**. I hurt my arm.

Put some ice on it, and rest for [[two days]].
What a bad day! You **missed** the bus this morning too.
Yes, and the **ticket machine** at the metro was broken!
Take care, and get well soon.

Can I go through that door?
No. It says **STAFF ONLY**. Only airport workers can go in.
Look, the sign says NO PHOTOS. You can't take photos here.
At the **gate**. There's a sign: PLEASE WAIT HERE.
That's an **EXIT** sign. In an **emergency**, **follow** the green signs.

lines: Uncle Faisal, how far is a **marathon**?
Wow! How did you **feel** after the race?
Tired, but very happy. I crossed the **finish line** in [[five]] hours.
What time do you get up?
At **dawn**. I run ten kilometres before work.
After **sunset**, I ride my **bike** in the park.
I eat **too many** **sweets**. Is that bad?
Yes. Don't eat **too much** sugar. Eat **smaller** meals and a lot of fruit.
Drink water. Then you have more **energy**.
OK! I'm going to walk ten thousand **steps** every day.

Every day, hundreds of planes **arrive** and **depart** here.
The holidays are starting. Many families are travelling.
Uncle, do you **remember** the old airport?
Yes. It was small, and it **closed** at night.

My **teenage** brother wants to work here. He's studying hard.
Good. He works hard, so he can **do well** and be **successful**.

I'm going to the **charity**. I'm a **volunteer** there.
We give food and **blankets** to **homeless** people and poor families.

Next month, I want to **donate** my old clothes.
Great idea! That can **cheer up** a lot of people.

Engines and aircraft. I **hope** to be a technician.
In [[2029]]. I'm going to get a **diploma** and an English **certificate**.
Great **plans**! What did you want to be when you were a child?
A pilot. But now I **imagine** a different **career**.
Maybe **one day**. First, I'm going to work in Riyadh.
I'm going to **apply** for a job at the airport **next month**.
